## DG6 round 1, code-security review: **FAIL**

**Candidate:** `sha256:7d6b4a9f…08cb` (2708 files, source `3cce3d4`), confirmed in a full clone and in both working copies. The repository HEAD moved during my run, but only to add the domain reviewer's records. The candidate didn't change, and I didn't read their records.

### Findings (F-DG6-120 to F-DG6-124)

| ID | Severity | Mandatory | Requirement | What happens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **F-DG6-120** | High | yes | REQ-S16-029 | A technical admin (ADM_TECH) can create a connector whose credential names any server environment variable, pointed at any https host. The connector test then sends the platform's own secret as a Bearer header to that host. Reproduced with `OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` (`secrets.ts:94`, `secret-refs.ts:47/108`, `http-pull.ts:112-118`). The `resolvable` field also shows which variables exist. The assistant, SMTP and S3 settings work the same way; I read those in the source but did not reproduce them. |
| **F-DG6-121** | High | yes | REQ-S10-002 | `GET /transformations/{id}/audit` ignores sensitivity. A Transformation Lead (TL) who gets 404 on a sensitive benefit reads all its events and the measured amount 987654.32 (`transformations/routes.ts:451-465`, `audit/index.ts:40-90`). |
| **F-DG6-122** | High | yes | REQ-S10-002 | `/api/v1/audit-events` redacts only the benefit's own events. Its measurement events, with their amounts, still reach an Auditor (AUD) who isn't admitted to the record (`audit/routes.ts:57-85`, `server.ts:536`). |
| **F-DG6-123** | High | yes | REQ-S10-002 | For a sensitive benefit, the form-record versions, comments and attachments answer 200 to a TL who gets 404 on the record itself. That includes a restricted comment's text, and the TL can still post comments (`forms/history.ts:41-51`, `comments.ts:113/169`, `attachments.ts:305`). |
| **F-DG6-124** | Low | no | REQ-S02-006 | A test defect, not a product one: the route-inventory sweep skips a table called `user_session`, but the table is `session` (`route-inventory.test.ts:107`). On a slow host the once-a-minute session touch makes "nothing persisted" cases fail spuriously. |

Each finding is reproduced; the test files are under `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/code-security/round-1/repro/`.

### Required checks (all ran)

- **Build, lint, format, openapi, no-cdn:** all exit 0. The contract has 932 operations. Lint and format failed on the first try because my own repro file was copied into the tree mid-run; the re-runs pass.
- **Typecheck:** exit 0 when run one package at a time. The two earlier runs were killed for lack of memory (exit 137), not for type errors.
- **Historical validators DG5, DG4, DG3, DG2, DG1:** all PASS in the repository tree. Runs in my sparse copy fail only on files I left out on purpose.
- **Unit tests on Node 22 and Node 24:** clean full runs exit 0 (2817, 2018 and 259 tests, with 2 skips by design). Node 22 here is v22.22.0, not the 22.22.2 the assignment states. The earlier runs under heavy load had timeouts, and each failing file then passed when run alone.
- **Integration, C.UTF-8:** 410 of 410 files pass, 4144 tests.
- **Integration, LANG unset:** 409 of 410 files pass. The one failing file is the F-DG6-124 test defect, and it passes when run alone.
  - Both integration runs were split into two shards, because a full run can't finish inside a background task's 2-hour limit on this host.
  - Earlier attempts are disclosed in the record: two runs were stopped at the time limit, one shard lost its worker process under load, and one run is void because it used an unbuilt copy.
- **Pending lists:** all empty. Migrations 0098–0123 are contiguous and were only added. The worker imports no API code. The secrets scan found only synthetic test values.

The verdict is FAIL because of the four unresolved High, mandatory findings. The disposable clones are removed, and no implementation file changed.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG6/round-1/`:
- `code-security-reviewer.json`
- `code-security-reviewer.findings.json`
